brief.subject: FTC sues Dollar General over register overcharges
brief.headline: Dollar General Sued for Charging More Than Shelf Prices; FTC Targets Toast Fees
brief.dek: The FTC and 20 states accuse Dollar General of overcharging at checkout, while a new suit targets hidden restaurant software fees.
brief.lede: The FTC and 20 states say Dollar General routinely charged shoppers more at the register than its shelf tags and ads showed. Check your receipt before you leave the store.

sections.heading: Dollar General accused of checkout overcharges
bullets: The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General on October 26 over deceptive pricing.
Regulators allege register prices often topped shelf tags, price labels and ads for years.
The alleged practice cost shoppers millions of dollars, according to the complaint.
Compare your receipt against shelf prices, especially on frequent small purchases where gaps are easy to miss.

sections.heading: Toast sued over hidden fees
bullets: The FTC, California officials and seven state attorneys general sued Toast Inc. today.
The suit alleges hidden and unauthorized fees plus deceptive subscription and cancellation practices.
Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Nebraska, Oklahoma and Utah joined the case.
Restaurant owners using the platform should review statements for charges they never agreed to.

sections.heading: FTC probes data-driven pricing
bullets: The FTC ordered nine major airlines, ride-sharing and food-delivery firms to hand over detailed information.
The agency wants to know how personal data may shape what consumers pay and what gig workers earn.
If you see different prices than others for the same ride or flight, this inquiry targets that practice.
